question: A company has a gearing ratio of 60% and an interest cover of 2.5 times. If operating profit increases by 20%, what is the new interest cover, assuming interest charges remain constant?
Under IAS 36, when should an entity test goodwill acquired in a business combination for impairment?
options: A. Only when there is an indication of impairment
B. Annually, regardless of whether there is any indication of impairment
C. Every five years regardless of indicators
D. Only when the subsidiary reports a loss

question: A company issues 10,000 convertible bonds at $100 each with a coupon rate of 5% per annum. The market rate for similar non-convertible bonds is 8%. Using the effective interest method, what is the initial carrying amount of the liability component? (PV annuity factor 8%, 5 years = 3.993; PV factor 8%, 5 years = 0.681)
Which of the following correctly describes the treatment of a revaluation surplus when a revalued asset is disposed of under IAS 16?
options: A. The revaluation surplus is transferred to retained earnings and recognised in profit or loss
B. The revaluation surplus may be transferred directly to retained earnings but is NOT recognised in profit or loss
C. The revaluation surplus must remain in equity indefinitely
D. The revaluation surplus is reversed through other comprehensive income upon disposal

question: In preparing a consolidated statement of financial position, a parent acquired 75% of a subsidiary for $450,000 when the subsidiary's net assets were $500,000 and the fair value of the non-controlling interest was $140,000. Using the full goodwill method, what is the goodwill recognised?
options: D. $215,000 – NCI share of net assets

question: Under IFRS 15, which of the following is the correct sequence for recognising revenue from contracts with customers?
options: A. Identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate transaction price, recognise revenue
B. Determine transaction price, identify contract, identify performance obligations, allocate, recognise
C. Identify performance obligations, identify contract, determine price, allocate, recognise
D. Identify contract, determine transaction price, identify performance obligations, allocate, recognise

question: A company has the following data: Sales $2,000,000; Variable costs 60% of sales; Fixed costs $500,000; Tax rate 30%. What is the degree of operating leverage (DOL) at the current sales level?
Which of the following statements about deferred tax under IAS 12 is CORRECT?
options: A. Deferred tax liabilities must always be discounted to present value
B. A deferred tax asset is recognised only to the extent that it is probable that future taxable profit will be available
C. Deferred tax is recognised on all temporary differences including those arising from initial recognition of goodwill
D. Deferred tax assets and liabilities may only be offset when they relate to the same tax authority and the entity has a legal right

question: In activity-based costing, an overhead absorption rate is calculated per cost driver. A company has setup costs of $120,000 and 400 setups. Product X requires 60 setups and produces 1,200 units. What is the setup overhead cost per unit of Product X?

A partnership has the following profit-sharing arrangements: salary to Partner A of $30,000, interest on capital of 5% (A: $100,000; B: $80,000), and residual profits shared 3:2. Net profit for the year is $95,000. What is Partner B's total share of profit?
Under IAS 37, a provision should be recognised when which of the following conditions are ALL met?
options: A. A present obligation exists, an outflow of resources is possible, and the amount can be estimated
B. A present obligation exists, an outflow of resources is probable, and a reliable estimate can be made
C. A constructive obligation exists, an outflow of resources is certain, and the timing is known
D. A legal obligation exists, an outflow of resources is probable, and the amount is material

question: A company uses the Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) model. Annual demand is 36,000 units, ordering cost is $50 per order, and holding cost is $2 per unit per annum. What is the EOQ?

In a hire purchase transaction, a buyer acquires an asset with a cash price of $80,000, paying a deposit of $20,000 and four annual instalments of $18,000. Using the sum-of-digits method for allocating finance charges, what is the finance charge allocated to Year 1?
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a finance lease under IFRS 16?
options: A. The lease transfers ownership of the asset to the lessee by the end of the lease term
B. The lessee has the option to purchase the asset at a price expected to be sufficiently lower than fair value
C. The present value of lease payments amounts to substantially all of the fair value of the asset
D. The lessor retains substantially all the risks and rewards incidental to ownership of the asset

question: A company is considering a project with an initial investment of $500,000. Expected net cash inflows are $150,000 per year for 5 years. The cost of capital is 10%. The NPV annuity factor at 10% for 5 years is 3.791 and at 15% is 3.352. What is the approximate IRR of the project?
